description:
An enterprise edge router in AS 65000 is already peered with an ISP in AS 65001. The ISP is learning the edge's internal prefixes as well as its public prefix. When the task is done, the ISP learns 192.0.2.0/24 from the edge (203.0.113.2) and no other prefix from the edge, and the edge advertises that same public prefix to the ISP and no other prefix. The internal prefixes that must not be advertised are 10.0.0.1/32, 10.1.0.0/30, and 10.2.0.0/30.

IP Addressing Plan:
- EDGE: eth1=203.0.113.2/30 (to ISP), eth2=10.1.0.1/30, eth3=10.2.0.1/30, lo=10.0.0.1/32
- ISP: eth1=203.0.113.1/30, lo=1.1.1.1/32
- INTERNAL1: eth1=10.1.0.2/30, lo=10.10.1.1/32
- INTERNAL2: eth1=10.2.0.2/30, lo=10.10.2.1/32

properties.description: EDGE advertises 192.0.2.0/24 to the ISP and no other prefix
ISP learns 192.0.2.0/24 from EDGE (203.0.113.2) and no other prefix from EDGE

preconfiguration.command:
vtysh -c 'conf t
 ip route 192.0.2.0/24 Null0
 ip prefix-list PL-PUBLIC-ONLY permit 192.0.2.0/24
 route-map FILTER-OUT permit 10
  match ip address prefix-list PL-PUBLIC-ONLY
 exit
 route-map ALLOW-ALL permit 10
 exit
 interface lo
  ip address 10.0.0.1/32
 exit
 interface eth1
  ip address 203.0.113.2/30
 exit
 interface eth2
  ip address 10.1.0.1/30
 exit
 interface eth3
  ip address 10.2.0.1/30
 exit
 router bgp 65000
  bgp router-id 10.0.0.1
  neighbor 203.0.113.1 remote-as 65001
  neighbor 203.0.113.1 route-map ALLOW-ALL in
  neighbor 203.0.113.1 route-map ALLOW-ALL out
  network 10.0.0.1/32
  network 10.1.0.0/30
  network 10.2.0.0/30
  network 192.0.2.0/24'

vtysh -c 'conf t
 route-map ALLOW-ALL permit 10
 exit
 interface lo
  ip address 1.1.1.1/32
 exit
 interface eth1
  ip address 203.0.113.1/30
 exit
 router bgp 65001
  bgp router-id 1.1.1.1
  neighbor 203.0.113.2 remote-as 65000
  neighbor 203.0.113.2 route-map ALLOW-ALL in
  neighbor 203.0.113.2 route-map ALLOW-ALL out'

vtysh -c 'conf t
 interface eth1
  ip address 10.1.0.2/30
 exit
 interface lo
  ip address 10.10.1.1/32
 exit'

vtysh -c 'conf t
 interface eth1
  ip address 10.2.0.2/30
 exit
 interface lo
  ip address 10.10.2.1/32
 exit'

fault_verification.description: EDGE's session to the ISP is Established
ISP has learned the internal prefix 10.0.0.1/32 from EDGE
FILTER-OUT is not the outgoing policy toward the ISP

optimal_solution.description: Confirm FILTER-OUT is not attached, apply it outbound on neighbor 203.0.113.1, then clear the session soft out and confirm the ISP holds only 192.0.2.0/24 from EDGE.

research_context.citation: BGP route filtering is a CCNP ENARSI and CCIE troubleshooting item. The injected fault is a route-map that is defined and not attached to the neighbor.
research_context.literature_basis: Prefix-lists and route-maps for outbound filtering are standard BGP policy, documented with RFC 4271. The authorized prefix is 192.0.2.0/24 (documentation prefix), distinct from the EDGE-ISP peering subnet.
research_context.time_justification: Thirty minutes covers reading the neighbor policy, attaching the existing route-map outbound, refreshing advertisements, and checking the ISP table.
